extracted.intended_audience: historians and readers interested in early 19th-century American Catholic missions and liturgical/missionary practice
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and describing normative practices, procedural rules, and ritual/administrative standards used by Father Charles Nerinckx in his early-19th-century missions (liturgical behavior, sacraments, community discipline, fundraising, and missionary organization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave cross size requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have every adult's grave adorned with a cross five feet high, and every child's with one of three feet, which the relations of the deceased must have in readiness before I perform the burial services."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family/relations must provide the specified cross sizes prior to burial; this is presented as a standard of burial decorum and part of the priest's practice for graves in his congregations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funeral procession devotions and graveside rites
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every Sunday and holiday, after Mass, I go in procession with the choir to the grave of the last deceased, where we sing the Miserere or the Dm Irat in English, at the close of which I make a short speech on death or prayers for the dead."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Mass processions to the last grave with sung prayers (Miserere or Dm Irat in English) followed by a short sermon; used regularly to mark burials and reinforce devotional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Communion retention, thanksgiving, and Rosary
rubrics_metrics.description: "Here, like every-where else, it was customary to run out of church immediately after Holy Communion. I have remedied this sad indifference toward the holiest of our mysteries, by assembling all those who approach the Holy Table, and reading aloud acts of thanksgiving, followed by the recitation of the Rosary to gain the indulgences."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prescriptive remedy for post-Communion indifference: assemble communicants, read acts of thanksgiving aloud, then recite the Rosary to obtain indulgences — instituted to foster devotion and decorum after Communion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparatory exercises for First Communion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Owing to the preparatory exercises which I introduced, first communion is received with much more devotion and fruit than heretofore."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation (catechesis/retreat-like exercises) before First Communion is required to increase devotion and spiritual benefit; presented as an effective pastoral standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage preparation and strict guest limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Persons who are about to enter the matrimonial state also have to prepare themselves by a retreat, before being admitted to it ... None are admitted to the wedding feast except parents, brothers, sisters, uncles, and aunts; no cousins or strangers, except the witnesses, can attend."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates for marriage must undergo a preparatory retreat; wedding feasts are tightly limited to immediate family and witnesses. The priest also prescribes devotional acts (see Rosary after sunset) to be performed by bride and groom and attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-wedding devotional practice (Rosary)
rubrics_metrics.description: "I direct the bride and bridegroom to say aloud with all those present at the feast, the whole Rosary immediately after sunset, and most of our catholics are faithful to my injunctions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of marital rites and community discipline, the priest orders the recitation of the entire Rosary aloud at the wedding feast's close to include Jesus and Mary symbolically and enforce devotional continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lenten and year-round abstinence/fasting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "Lard in the preparation of food is allowed every day, but we have to abstain from meat the first four days of Lent, the entire Holy Week, and on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Saturdays of every week. ... On the days that meat is allowed, we can use only one kind and one course, a practice that is kept up the whole year round, although it is not ordered by the church."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local/regional fasting regimen: specific days of meat abstinence and a stricter household rule limiting meat-days to one kind and one course year-round (a local pastoral discipline beyond formal church law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nightly and morning common prayers; Litany practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every night, and in every house, besides the customary evening prayers, which are said in common the whole year through, even in the houses of mixed catholics, they say the Litany of all the Saints, and, if they can not read, the Rosary. Since New Year's, we have encouraged our people to come together every morning before daylight, and say the prayers aloud in common, a pious practice which many follow."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes communal domestic devotions: evening prayers plus Litany of All Saints (or Rosary if illiterate), and encouraged early-morning communal prayer aloud; framed as pastoral encouragement to sustain piety in households.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corpus Christi procession organization and ceremonial roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed account: "Three men on horseback opened the march, the middle one carrying a silk flag surmounted by a large cross, the two others holding huge green boughs ... an acolyte ... with the processional cross, heading the double row ... canopy ... held aloft by four men, and immediately behind the Blessed Sacrament followed fourteen armed men, led by a uniformed sergeant. Three other men on horseback, also-uniformed, with drawn swords, brought up the rear, and held back the surging crowd ... Choirs of men and women sung alternately ... a squad of horsemen acting as marshals saw that every thing proceeded in an orderly manner."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the composition, sequence, and roles in public processions (flag-bearers, acolyte, canopy-bearers, armed escorts, choirs, marshals). Emphasizes order, decorum, and the evangelizing effect of ceremonial splendor on sectarians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public rites and ceremonies as evangelization
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our rites and ceremonies exert a powerful influence upon sectarians, many of whom are favorably impressed by them, and are led to investigate the claims of the catholic church on their allegiance, and are led into its fold."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates deliberate use of elaborate public worship and processions as a means of attracting and converting non-Catholics; ceremonial beauty and order are presented as pastoral strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of racing and secular amusements; prohibition on balls/dances
rubrics_metrics.description: "The great pastime of our population consists in racing, the horses running for premiums, and they take great delight in it. It is often attended by deathly accidents and is the source of many sins. It is hard to keep our catholics from these amusements, but they have given up balls and dances, which are, however, much frequented by non-catholics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pastoral stance: actively discourage dangerous or sinful amusements (racing); promote abandonment of balls and dances among parishioners while noting non-Catholics continue such entertainments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction and reception procedure for converts
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have at present some twenty persons, white and black, under instruction who desire to join the church; I have received several this year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires catechetical instruction for converts of all backgrounds before reception; the practice of keeping candidates under instruction is a normative catechetical standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission to public penance for civilly married couples
rubrics_metrics.description: "Five or six couples, who were married out of the church, have begged to be admitted to public penance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Couples married outside the Church may be admitted to public penance (a remedial pastoral process) before full reconciliation and integration into sacramental life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church building, altar design, land acquisition and fundraising practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Several passages: "I have finally succeeded in making the contract for an altar which is to cost $160, part of which I defray myself. Made after my own designs, it will be inlaid with different kinds of wood, and have a niche flanked with columns, in which I intend to place my statue of the Blessed Virgin ... I have charged two catholic gentlemen to buy a lot or farm in my name to build a church ... they are already circulating subscription lists to enable them to build three churches ... Captain John Hanley gives to the church four hundred acres ... N. Beiti ... offers two hundred acres ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clergy-led initiatives for material provisioning: contracting altars to personal design, clergy contributing funds, soliciting subscriptions, arranging land grants and purchases in the priest's name, and coordinating benefactors to secure land for churches and connected institutions (e.g., schools). Presented as standard missionary-administrative practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking land grants to educational institutions (school for girls)
rubrics_metrics.description: "I would like to have a school for girls connected with it, and he once before offered that much to the sisters of the congregation of the Blessed Virgin Mary."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferentially ties land and church endowments to founding schools and inviting religious sisters for education; establishing schools is presented as a mission priority and criterion for land-use decisions.
